To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Kaposi sarcomas virus vIRF-1 interacts with MM1alpha and stimulates transcriptional activity of c-Myc in PEL cells.

the viral interferon regulatory factor vIRF- 3 of Kaposis sarcoma-associated herpes virus can associate with the cellular protein MM-1alpha, which in turn binds to the c-Myc protein and inhibits c-Myc transcription.
vIRF3, a viral protein expressed by KSHV, interacts with MM1alpha, a cellular protein that negatively regulates c-Myc function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel mechanism for vIRF- 3-mediated stimulation of c-Myc-dependent gene transcription in PEL.
the role of viral homologue of interferon regulatory factors in the development of lymphoproliferation associated with Kaposi sarcomas-associated herpesvirus.
the identification and characterization of novel vIRF-1 and vIRF-2 interacting proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vIRF3 is able to interact with MM1alpha and inhibit the MM1alpha-c-Myc interaction.
the vIRF3-c-Myc interaction is a key step in the development of lymphoproliferation in PEL and other lymphoproliferations.
vIRF3 is a viral protein that can stimulate c-myc transcriptional activity and thereby contribute to deregulation of B-cell proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

KSHV-encoded vIRF-1, vIRF2, and vIRF3 proteins can interact with the MM1alpha protein, a known negative regulator of c-Myc, and thereby stimulate c-Myc-mediated gene transcription in the context of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpes virus (KSHV)-infected cells.
vIRF proteins can be considered as a novel group of viral oncogenes that contribute to the lymphomagenesis by deregulating the function of c-Myc.
vIRF proteins are important for Kaposi sarcomas-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) pathogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vIRF3 protein is capable of interacting with cellular proteins and that it can modulate cellular gene expression in PEL cells.
KSHV vIRF- 3 protein interacts with MM1alpha, which is an endogenous suppressor of the proto-oncogene c-Myc.

vIRF3 can stimulate c-Myc-dependent activation of the cdk4 gene, a key regulator of the cell cycle, and that vIRF1, vIRF2, and vIRF3 all can bind to the cellular interferon regulatory factor-3 protein.
